# On the Bezrukavnikov-Kaledin quantization of symplectic varieties in characteristic $p$

**Authors:** Ekaterina Bogdanova Address: National Research University “Higher School of Economics”, Russia Email address: katbogd11@gmail.com and Vadim Vologodsky Address: National Research University “Higher School of Economics”, Russia Email address: vologod@gmail.com

## Abstract

We prove that after inverting the Planck constant $h$ the Bezrukavnikov-Kaledin quantization $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h})$ of symplectic variety $X$ in characteristic $p$ with $H^{2}(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{X})=0$ is Morita equivalent to a certain central reduction of the algebra of differential operators on $X$ .

## 1. Introduction

### 1.1. Frobenius-constant quantizations.

For the duration of this paper, let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>2$ . Given a scheme $X$ over $k$ we denote by $X^{\prime}$ the Frobenius twist of $X$ and by $F:X\to X^{\prime}$ the $k$ -linear Frobenius morphism. Since $F$ is a homeomorphism on the underlying topological spaces we shall identify the categories of sheaves on $X$ and $X^{\prime}$ .

Let $X$ be a smooth variety over $k$ equipped with a symplectic $2$ -form $\omega$ . Recall, that a quantization $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h})$ of $(X,\omega)$ is a sheaf ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}$ on the Zariski site of $X$ of flat $k[[h]]$ -algebras complete with respect to the $h$ -adic topology together with an isomorphism of $k$ -algebras

$$ {\mathcal{O}}_{h}/h\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{O}}_{X} $$

such that, for any two local sections $\tilde{f}$ , $\tilde{g}$ of ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}$ , one has

$$ \{f,g\}\equiv\frac{\tilde{f}\tilde{g}-\tilde{g}\tilde{f}}{h}\operatorname{mod}h. $$

Here $f$ and $g$ stand for the images in ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ of $\tilde{f}$ and $\tilde{g}$ respectively and $\{,\}$ for the Poisson bracket ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ induced by the symplectic structure. Note that if $X$ is affine then giving a quantization $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h})$ of $(X,\omega)$ is equivalent to giving a quantization ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}(X)$ of the Poisson algebra ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}(X)$ (see e.g. [BK1, Remark 1.6]).

A feature special to characteristic $p$ is that the Poisson algebra ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ of a symplectic variety has a large center consisting of $p$ -th powers of functions. We are going to identify it with the sheaf ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}$ using the Frobenius morphism

$$ F^{*}:{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}^{p}\subset{\mathcal{O}}_{X}. $$

Given a quantization $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h})$ of $(X,\omega)$ we have $k$ -linear homomorphisms

$$ {\mathcal{Z}}_{h}\twoheadrightarrow{\mathcal{Z}}_{h}/h\hookrightarrow{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}. $$

from the center ${\mathcal{Z}}_{h}$ of the quantization ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}$ to the Poisson center. Following [BK3], a quantization is called central if the composition (1.1) is surjective. A Frobenius-constant quantization of $(X,\omega)$ is a pair consisting of a quantization $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h})$ of the symplectic variety $X$ together with a $k[[h]]$ -algebra isomorphism

$$ s:{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]]\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{Z}}_{h} $$

such that, for any local section $f^{p}\in{\mathcal{O}}_{X}^{p}={\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}\subset{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]]$ and a lift $\tilde{f}\in{\mathcal{O}}_{h}$ of $f\in{\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ , one has that11 1 Recall, that for any associative algebra $A$ over a field of characteristic $p$ and every elements $x,y\in A$ , the element $(x+y)^{p}-x^{p}-y^{p}$ can be written as a homogeneous Lie polynomial in $x$ and $y$ of degree $p$ . Applying this to $A={\mathcal{O}}_{h}$ we infer that $\tilde{f}^{p}\mod h^{p}$ depends only on $f\in{\mathcal{O}}_{h}/h$ and not on the choice of a lifting $\tilde{f}\in{\mathcal{O}}_{h}$ of $f$ . Also, using that, for any $x\in A$ , one has that $\ad_{x^{p}}=(\ad_{x})^{p}:A\to A$ , it follows that $\tilde{f}^{p}$ is a central element of ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}/h^{p}$ .

$$ s(f^{p})=\tilde{f}^{p}\mod h^{p-1}. $$

It is clear that a quantization that admits a Frobenius-constant structure is central.

A Frobenius-constant structure on $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h})$ makes ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}$ into a sheaf of algebras over ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]]$ . It is shown in [BK3] that ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}$ is locally free of rank $p^{\dim X}$ as an ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]]$ -module for the Zariski topology on $X^{\prime}$ .

Frobenius-constant quantizations of symplectic varieties have been first introduced by Bezrukavnikov and Kaledin as a tool for proving the categorical McKay correspondence for symplectic resolutions of singularities (see [BK2]). Most of the foundational results have been obtained in [BK3]. The technique introduced in [BK2] has found some other applications in geometric representations theory (see e.g., [BF], [BL]). A key to all these applications is the Azumaya property of the algebra ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}(h^{-1})$ obtained from ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}$ by inverting $h$ : it is shown in [BK3] that for any Frobenius-constant quantization on $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h})$ , the algebra ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}(h^{-1})$ is isomorphic, that is locally, for the fppf topology on $X^{\prime}$ , to a matrix algebra over ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}((h))$ . Since the algebra ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}$ has no zero divisors ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}(h^{-1})$ does not split even locally for the étale topology on $X^{\prime}$ (unless $\dim X=0$ ). In [BK3, Proposition 1.24] a formula for the class of this Azumaya algebra in an appropriate Brauer group was proposed. However, it has been observed in [M] that the formula in [BK3] is not correct as stated. The immediate goal of this paper is to correct it. The technique introduced along its proof (in particular, the Basic Lemma from §1.8) plays an essential role in a sequel paper joint with Kubrak and Travkin [BKTV], where we prove that the category of quasi-coherent sheaves on any restricted symplectic variety admits a canonical Frobenius-constant quantization.

### 1.2. Differential operators as a Frobenius-constant quantization.

A basic example of a Frobenius-constant quantization is the following. Let $Y$ be a smooth variety over $k$ , $X:={\mathbb{T}}^{*}_{Y}$ the cotangent bundle to $Y$ equipped with the canonical symplectic structure $\omega$ . Denote by $D_{Y}$ the sheaf of differential operators on $Y$ . This comes with a filtration given by the order of a differential operator. Applying the Rees construction to the filtered algebra $D_{Y}$ we obtain a sheaf of algebras $D_{Y,h}$ flat over $k[h]$ whose fiber over $h=1$ is $D_{Y}$ and whose fiber over $h=0$ is the symmetric algebra $S^{\cdot}T_{Y}$ . Explicitly, $D_{Y,h}$ is the subalgebra of $D_{Y}[h]$ generated by $h$ , ${\mathcal{O}}_{Y}$ , and $hT_{Y}$ . The $p$ -curvature homomorphism

$$ S^{\cdot}T_{Y^{\prime}}\to D_{Y,h} $$

sending a function $f\in{\mathcal{O}}_{Y}$ to $f^{p}$ and a vector field $\theta\in T_{Y}$ to $(h\theta)^{p}-h^{p-1}(h\theta^{[p]})$ induces an isomorphism between the algebra $S^{\cdot}T_{Y^{\prime}}[h]$ and the center of $D_{Y,h}$ . In particular, $D_{Y,h}$ can be viewed as a quasi-coherent sheaf on ${\mathbb{T}}_{Y^{\prime}}^{*}$ . The canonical Frobenius-constant quantization of $({\mathbb{T}}^{*}_{Y},\omega)$ is obtained from $D_{Y,h}$ by $h$ -completion. We shall denote this canonical Frobenius-constant quantization of $({\mathbb{T}}^{*}_{Y},\omega)$ by $({\mathbb{T}}^{*}_{Y},{\mathcal{D}}_{Y,h})$ .

### 1.3. Restricted Poisson structures.

There is a local obstruction to the existence of a central quantization of a symplectic variety $(X,\omega)$ . It is observed in [BK3] that if $f^{p}\in{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}^{p}$ is in the image (1.1) then the restricted power $H_{f}^{[p]}$ of the Hamiltonian vector field $H_{f}$ is again Hamiltonian: $H_{f}^{[p]}=H_{f^{[p]}}$ for some $f^{[p]}\in{\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ . For example, it follows that the torus $({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times{\mathbb{G}}_{m},\omega=\frac{dx}{x}\wedge\frac{dy}{y})$ does not admit central quantizations.

A Frobenius-constant structure on $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h})$ provides a canonical Hamiltonian for $H_{f}^{[p]}$ . In fact, given a Frobenius-constant quantization $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s)$ the formula

$$ f^{[p]}=\frac{1}{h^{p-1}}(\tilde{f}^{p}-s(f))\mod h $$

defines a restricted structure on the Poisson algebra ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ , that is the structure of a restricted Lie algebra on ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ such that $(f^{2})^{[p]}=2f^{[p]}f^{p}$ and $H_{f}^{[p]}=H_{f^{[p]}}$ 22 2 Whereas the notion of restricted Lie algebra goes back to Jacobson (1937), the concept of restricted Poisson algebra is an invention of Bezrukavnikov and Kaledin ([BK3, Def. 1.9]). Note that using the identity $fg=\frac{1}{4}((f+g)^{2}-(f-g)^{2})$ , one has that $(fg)^{[p]}=f^{p}g^{[p]}+f^{[p]}g^{p}+P(f,g)$ , where $P(f,g)$ is an element of a free Poisson algebra on $f$ and $g$ . In [BK3], the authors construct $P(f,g)$ explicitly in any characteristic which makes it possible to define the notion of restricted Poisson algebra even in characteristic $2$ ..

It is shown in [BK3] that, for every symplectic variety $(X,\omega)$ , giving a restricted Poisson structure on ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ is equivalent to giving a class

$$ [\eta]\in H^{0}_{Zar}(X,\coker({\mathcal{O}}_{X}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle d}}{{\longrightarrow}}\Omega^{1}_{X})) $$

such that

$$ d([\eta])=\omega. $$

In one direction, if $\eta\in\Omega^{1}_{X}$ , $d\eta=\omega$ , then the formula

$$ f^{[p]}=L^{p-1}_{H_{f}}\iota_{H_{f}}\eta-\iota_{H_{f}^{[p]}}\eta $$

defines a restricted structure on ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ . In particular, if $(X,\omega)$ admits a restricted structure then $\omega$ is exact locally for Zariski topology on $X$ .

### 1.4. Classification of Frobenius-constant quantizations.

Fix a symplectic variety $X$ with a restricted Poisson structure $[\eta]$ . Denote by $Q(X,[\eta])$ the set of isomorphism classes of Frobenius-constant quantizations $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s)$ compatible with $[\eta]$ . In [BK3], Bezrukavnikov and Kaledin constructed a map of sets

$$ \rho:Q(X,[\eta])\to H^{1}_{et}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*p}) $$

and showed that if $H^{1}_{Zar}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{p})=0$ then $\rho$ is injective and if $H^{2}_{Zar}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{p})=0$ then $\rho$ is surjective. Consequently, if both cohomology groups vanish the map $\rho$ is a bijection and there is a canonical Frobenius-constant quantization of $(X,[\eta])$ corresponding to $0\in H^{1}_{et}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*p})$ . This quantization $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s)$ is uniquely characterized as the one that admits a ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$ -equivariant structure: an isomorphism ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]]$ -algebras

$$ \alpha:{\mathcal{O}}_{-h}^{op}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{O}}_{h} $$

identical modulo $h$ and such that $\alpha\circ\alpha=\Id$ . We review the construction of $\rho$ in §2.

### 1.5. A central reduction of the algebra of differential operators.

A class

$$ [\eta]\in H_{Zar}^{0}\left(X,\operatorname{coker}\left(\mathcal{O}_{X}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle d}}{{\longrightarrow}}\Omega_{X}^{1}\right)\right) $$

gives rise to a certain central reduction $\mathcal{D}_{X,[\eta],h}$ of the algebra $\mathcal{D}_{X,h}$ . We first construct this reduction locally and then glue. For any open subset $U$ together with a $1$ -form $\eta\in\Omega^{1}(U)$ representing $[\eta]$ , consider the graph $\Gamma_{\eta}:U^{\prime}\rightarrow\mathbb{T}_{U^{\prime}}^{*}$ of $\eta\otimes 1\in\Omega^{1}(U^{\prime})$ . Let $\mathcal{D}_{U,h}$ be the quantization of $\mathbb{T}^{*}_{U}$ defined above regarded as a locally free sheaf of modules over $S^{\cdot}T_{U^{\prime}}[[h]]$ on $U$ . Set

$$ \Gamma_{\eta_{1}}^{*}\mathcal{D}_{U,h}=\mathcal{D}_{U,h}/I_{\Gamma_{\eta}}\mathcal{D}_{U,h}. $$

Here $I_{\Gamma_{\eta}}\subset S^{\cdot}T_{U^{\prime}}$ is sheaf of ideals defined by the closed embedding $\Gamma_{\eta}$ . Note that $\Gamma_{\eta_{1}}^{*}\mathcal{D}_{U,h}$ is a sheaf of algebras over $S^{\cdot}T_{U^{\prime}}/I_{\Gamma_{\eta}}[[h]]\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{O}}_{U^{\prime}}[[h]]$ .

Suppose we are given two forms $\eta_{1}$ , $\eta_{2}$ on $U$ representing the class $[\eta]$ . Let us construct a canonical isomorphism between the algebras $\Gamma_{\eta_{1}}^{*}\mathcal{D}_{X,h}$ and $\Gamma_{\eta_{2}}^{*}\mathcal{D}_{X,h}$ . Set $\mu=\eta_{1}-\eta_{2}$ . Define the automorphism $\phi_{\mu}$ of $\mathcal{D}_{X,h}$ by setting $\phi_{\mu}(f)=f$ and $\phi_{\mu}(h\theta)=h\theta+\iota_{\theta}\mu$ , for any function $f$ and vector field $\theta$ 33 3 Informally, this isomorphism is the conjugation by $e^{\frac{1}{h}\int\mu}$ .. Let $t_{\mu}$ be the translation by $\mu$ on $S^{\cdot}T_{U^{\prime}}$ i.e., an automorphism sending a vector field $\theta$ to $\theta+\iota_{\theta}\mu$ . Then using the Katz formula [Katz, §7.22] (and the exactness of $\mu$ ) the following diagram is commutative

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{O}_{U^{\prime}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces S^{\cdot}T_{U^{\prime}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}_{U,h}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces S^{\cdot}T_{U^{\prime}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}_{U,h}.} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma_{\eta_{1}}^{*}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces s} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces t_{\mu}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi_{\mu}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma_{\eta_{2}}^{*}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces s} $$

The desired isomorphism is given by the formula

$$ \Gamma_{\eta_{1}}^{*}\mathcal{D}_{U,h}=\mathcal{D}_{U,h}\otimes_{S^{\cdot}T_{U^{\prime}}}S^{\cdot}T_{U^{\prime}}/\penalty\mathcal{I}_{\Gamma_{\eta_{1}}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\phi_{\mu}\otimes t_{\mu}}}{{\longrightarrow}}\mathcal{D}_{U,h}\otimes_{S^{\cdot}T_{U^{\prime}}}S^{\cdot}T_{U^{\prime}}/\penalty\mathcal{I}_{\Gamma_{\eta_{2}}}=\Gamma_{\eta_{2}}^{*}\mathcal{D}_{U,h}. $$

Given three $1$ -forms $\eta_{1}$ , $\eta_{2}$ , and $\eta_{3}$ representing the class $[\eta]$ one has

$$ (\phi_{\eta_{1}-\eta_{2}}\otimes t_{\eta_{1}-\eta_{2}})\circ(\phi_{\eta_{2}-\eta_{3}}\otimes t_{\eta_{2}-\eta_{3}})=\phi_{\eta_{1}-\eta_{3}}\otimes t_{\eta_{1}-\eta_{3}}. $$

The sheaf of algebras $\mathcal{D}_{X,[\eta],h}$ is obtained by gluing $\Gamma_{\eta}^{*}\mathcal{D}_{U,h}$ along the above isomorphisms.

The sheaf ${\mathcal{D}}_{X,[\eta],h}$ of ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]]$ -algebras is locally free as a ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]]$ -module of rank $p^{2\dim X}$ . The commutative algebra ${\mathcal{D}}_{X,[\eta],h}/h$ is isomorphic to the algebra of functions on the Frobenius neighborhood of the zero section $X\hookrightarrow{\mathbb{T}}^{*}_{X}$ with the Poisson structure given by the symplectic form $\omega_{can}+\proj^{*}\omega$ on ${\mathbb{T}}^{*}_{X}$ . Here $\omega_{can}$ is the canonical symplectic form on the cotangent bundle, and $\proj:{\mathbb{T}}^{*}_{X}\to X$ is the projection.

#### Remark 1.1.

The sheaf $\mathcal{D}_{X,[\eta],h}$ is the restriction of a certain canonical locally free ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}\times{\mathbb{P}}^{1}}$ -algebra over $X^{\prime}\times{\mathbb{P}}^{1}$ to the formal completion of $X^{\prime}\times\{0\}\hookrightarrow X^{\prime}\times{\mathbb{P}}^{1}$ ([BKTV] §3.3).

### 1.6. Main result.

Denote by $\operatorname{Br}(X^{\prime}[[h]])$ the Brauer group of the formal scheme $(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]])$ obtained from $X^{\prime}\times\Spec k[h]$ by completion along the closed subscheme cut by the equation $h=0$ . We have homomorphisms:

$$ \delta\colon H^{1}_{et}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*p})\to H^{2}_{et}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*})\cong\operatorname{Br}(X^{\prime})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Br}(X^{\prime}[[h]]). $$

The first map in (1.7) is the boundary morphism associated to the short exact sequence of sheaves for the étale topology

$$ 0\to{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle p}}{{\longrightarrow}}{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle}}{{\longrightarrow}}{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*p}\to 0. $$

The right arrow in (1.7) is the pullback homomorphism which is a split injection because its composition with the restriction homomorphism

$$ i^{*}\colon\operatorname{Br}(X^{\prime}[[h]])\to\operatorname{Br}(X^{\prime}) $$

is the identity. Given a class $\gamma\in H^{1}_{et}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*p})$ we denote by $\delta(\gamma)\in\operatorname{Br}(X^{\prime}[[h]])$ the image of $\gamma$ under the composition (1.7). Finally, we can state the main result of this paper.

#### Theorem 1.

Let $(X,\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic variety of dimension $2n$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$ , and let $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s)$ be a Frobenius-constant quantization of $(X,\omega)$ . Denote by $[\eta]\in H^{0}_{Zar}(X,\coker({\mathcal{O}}_{X}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle d}}{{\longrightarrow}}\Omega^{1}_{X}))$ the restricted Poisson structure corresponding to $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s)$ and by $\gamma=\rho(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s)\in H^{1}_{et}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*p})$ the image of $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s)$ under (1.4). Then there exists an Azumaya algebra ${\mathcal{O}}^{\sharp}_{h}$ over the formal scheme $(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]])$ with the following properties:

- (i) There exists an isomorphism of ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}((h))$ -algebras (1.8)

$$ ({\mathcal{O}}_{h}\otimes_{{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]]}{\mathcal{D}}_{X,[\eta],h}^{op})(h^{-1})\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{O}}^{\sharp}_{h}(h^{-1}) $$

- (ii) We have that (1.9)

$$ i^{*}[{\mathcal{O}}^{\sharp}_{h}]=i^{*}(\delta(\gamma)). $$

In partucular, if $H^{2}(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{X})=0$ then $[{\mathcal{O}}^{\sharp}_{h}]=\delta(\gamma)$ .

In particular, let $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s)$ be a Frobenius-constant quantization that admits ${\mathbb{Z}}/2{\mathbb{Z}}$ -equivariant structure (1.5). Assume that $H^{2}(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{X})=0$ . Then by Theorem 1 ${\mathcal{O}}^{\sharp}_{h}$ is a split Azumaya algebra, that is there exists a locally free ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]]$ -module $E$ of finite rank and an isomorphism of ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]]$ -algebras

$$ {\mathcal{O}}^{\sharp}_{h}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\End_{{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]]}(E). $$

Using (1.8) and the Azumaya property of ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}(h^{-1})$ and ${\mathcal{D}}_{X,[\eta],h}(h^{-1})$ we observe an equivalence of categories

$$ \Mod({\mathcal{D}}_{X,[\eta],h}(h^{-1}))\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\Mod({\mathcal{O}}_{h}(h^{-1})) $$

between the category of ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}(h^{-1})$ -modules and the category of ${\mathcal{D}}_{X,[\eta],h}(h^{-1})$ -modules. The functor from left to right carries a ${\mathcal{D}}_{X,[\eta],h}(h^{-1})$ -module $M$ to $E\otimes_{{\mathcal{D}}_{X,[\eta],h}}M$ ; the quasi-inverse functor takes an ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}(h^{-1})$ -module $N$ to ${{\mathcal{H}}}om_{{\mathcal{O}}_{h}}(E,N)$ .

Also note that if $H^{1}_{Zar}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{p})=0$ then the map

$$ H^{0}(X,\Omega^{1}_{X})\to H^{0}_{Zar}(X,\coker({\mathcal{O}}_{X}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle d}}{{\longrightarrow}}\Omega^{1}_{X})) $$

is surjective and, thus, any restricted Poisson structure arises from a global $1$ -form $\eta$ . In this case objects of $\Mod({\mathcal{D}}_{X,[\eta],h}(h^{-1}))$ can be viewed as ${\mathcal{D}}_{X,h}(h^{-1})$ -modules whose $p$ -curvature equals $\eta$ .

### 1.7. ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant quantizations.

Let $(X,\omega)$ be a symplectic variety equipped with an action

$$ \lambda\colon{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X\to X $$

of the multiplicative group such that $\omega$ has a positive weight $m$ with respect to this action. Moreover, we shall assume that $m$ invertible in $k$ . Denote by $\theta$ the Euler vector field on $X$ corresponding to the ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -action. Then the formula $\eta=\frac{1}{m}\iota_{\theta}\omega$ defines a restricted structure on $X$ . Define a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -action on $X^{\prime}$ twisting (1.11) by the $p$ -th power map ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle F}}{{\longrightarrow}}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . Also let ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ act on $X^{\prime}[h]:=X^{\prime}\times\Spec k[h]$ as above on the first factor and by $z*h=z^{m}h$ on the second one.

A ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant Frobenius-constant quantization of $X$ is a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant sheaf $O_{h}$ of associative ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}[h]}$ -algebras on $X^{\prime}[h]$ , locally free as an ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}[h]}$ -module, such that the restriction ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}$ of $O_{h}$ to the formal completion of $X^{\prime}[h]$ along the divisor $h=0$ is a Frobenius-constant quantization of $X$ compatible with the restricted structure $[\eta]$ . Examples of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant quantizations arise in geometric representation theory (see e.g., [BK2], [BF], [BL], [KT]).

Assume that morphism (1.11) extends to a morphism

$$ \tilde{\lambda}:{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\times X\to X. $$

Then the restriction of $O_{h}$ to the open subscheme $X^{\prime}[h,h^{-1}]\hookrightarrow X^{\prime}[h]$ is an Azumaya algebra. As an application of Theorem 1 we prove in §5 a conjecture of Kubrak-Travkin concerning the class of this algebra in the Brauer group. Namely, we show that, for every ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant Frobenius-constant quantization $O_{h}$ , the following equality in $\operatorname{Br}(X^{\prime})$ holds

$$ [O_{h=1}]=[\frac{1}{m}\eta]+\tilde{\lambda}_{0}^{*}[\rho(O_{h})]. $$

Here $[\eta]$ stands for the image of $\eta$ under the canonical map $\Gamma(X^{\prime},\Omega^{1}_{X^{\prime}})\to\operatorname{Br}(X^{\prime})$ , $\rho(O_{h})\in H^{1}_{et}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*p})$ for the class associated to the formal quantization via (1.4), and $[\rho(O_{h})]$ for its image in the Brauer group.

### 1.8. Plan of the proof.

Using the language of formal geometry we reduce the theorem to a group-theoretic statement. We shall start by explaining the latter.

Let $(V,\omega_{V})$ be a finite-dimensional symplectic vector space over $k$ , and let $A_{h}$ be the algebra over $k[[h]]$ generated by the dual vector space $V^{*}$ subject to the relations

$$ fg-gf=\omega_{V}^{-1}(f,g)h,\quad f^{p}=0 $$

for any $f,g\in V^{*}$ . We refer to $A_{h}$ as the restricted Weyl algebra. This is a flat $k[[h]]$ -algebra whose reduction modulo $h$ is the finite-dimensional commutative algebra of functions on the Frobenius neighborhood of the origin in the affine space $\Spec(S^{\cdot}V^{*}):=\bf{V}$ . Explicitly, $A_{0}:=S^{\cdot}V^{*}/J_{V}$ where $J_{V}$ is the ideal generated by $f^{p}$ for all $f\in V^{*}$ . The quantization $A_{h}$ of $A_{0}$ specifies a restricted Poisson structure $[\eta_{V}]\in\coker(A_{0}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle d}}{{\longrightarrow}}\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}})$ .44 4 Explicitly $[\eta_{V}]$ is characterized as a unique homogeneous class such that $d[\eta_{V}]=\omega_{V}$ .

Denote by $G$ the group scheme $\underline{\Aut}(A_{h})$ of $k[[h]]$ -linear automorphisms of the algebra $A_{h}$ , by $G^{\geq 1}$ the subgroup of automorphisms identical modulo $h$ , and by $G_{0}$ the quotient of $G$ by $G^{\geq 1}$ . As shown in [BK3], $G_{0}$ is the group scheme of automorphisms of $A_{0}$ preserving the class $[\eta_{V}]$ .

A pair $(W,W^{*})$ of transversal Lagrangian subspaces of $V$ defines an isomorphism between the algebra $A_{h}(h^{-1})$ and the matrix algebra $\End_{k}(S^{\cdot}W^{*}/J_{W})((h))$ which, in turn, gives an embedding $G\hookrightarrow L\PGL(p^{n})$ , where $L\PGL(p^{n})$ is the loop group of $\PGL(p^{n})$ (viewed as a sheaf for the fpqc topology). Then the extension

### 1.9. Further directions.

In this subsection we briefly discuss some applications of Theorem 1 obtained in a sequel paper joint with Dmitry Kubrak and Roman Travkin [BKTV].

According to the Bezrukavnikov-Kaledin theorem from §1.4 every smooth affine restricted symplectic variety admits a unique up to a non-canonical isomorphism Frobenius-constant quantization $O_{h}$ with $\rho[O_{h}]=0$ . Moreover, using Remark 1.1 and equivalence (1.10) we extend the range of quantum parameter $h$ from being a formal variable to a genuine coordinate on ${\mathbb{P}}^{1}$ . ## 2. Review of the Bezrukavnikov-Kaledin construction

For reader’s convenience we review the Bezrukavnikov-Kaledin construction of quantizations. We also introduce some notations to be used later. Nothing in this section is an invention of the authors.

### 2.1. Darboux Lemma in characteristic $p$ .

Our proof of Theorem 1, as well as the Bezrukavnikov-Kaledin construction of quantizations, is based on a version of the Gelfand-Kazhdan formal geometry that makes it possible to localize the problem and ultimately reduce it to a statement in group theory. The main idea is as follows. For a symplectic variety $X$ , the Poisson bracket on ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ is ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}$ -linear. Therefore, we can view $X$ as a Poisson scheme over $X^{\prime}$ . For any restricted structure on ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ , one has ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{[p]}=0$ . Therefore, a symplectic variety $X$ with a restricted structure can be viewed as a restricted Poisson scheme over $X^{\prime}$ . Consider the constant restricted Poisson scheme over $X^{\prime}$ :

$$ X^{\prime}\times\Spec A_{0}\to X^{\prime}, $$

where

$$ A_{0}=k[x_{1},y_{1},\cdots,x_{n},y_{n}]/(x_{1}^{p},y_{1}^{p},\cdots,x_{n}^{p},y_{n}^{p}) $$

$2n=\dim X$ , the morphism (2.1) is the projection to the first factor, the Poisson structure is given by symplectic form $\sum_{i}dy_{i}\wedge dx_{i}$ , and the restricted structure is determined by $x_{i}^{[p]}=y_{i}^{[p]}=0$ . A key insight of Bezrukavnikov and Kaledin is that any smooth symplectic variety $X$ with a restricted structure, viewed as a restricted Poisson scheme over $X^{\prime}$ , is locally for the fpqc topology on $X^{\prime}$ isomorphic to the constant restricted Poisson scheme $X^{\prime}\times\Spec A_{0}\to X^{\prime}$ . This is an analogue of the Darboux Lemma.

### 2.2. Quantum Darboux Lemma.

There is also a quantum version of the Darboux Lemma proven in [BK3]: for any Frobenius-constant quantization $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s)$ , the sheaf of associative ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]]$ -algebras ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}$ is isomorphic locally for the fpqc topology on $X^{\prime}$ to the $h$ -completed tensor product ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}\otimes_{k}A_{h}$ , where $A_{h}$ is the reduced Weyl algebra that is the $k[[h]]$ -algebra generated by variable $x_{i},y_{i}$ , $(1\leq i,j,\leq n)$ , subject to the relations

$$ y_{j}x_{i}-x_{i}y_{j}=\delta_{ij}h,\quad x_{i}^{p}=y_{i}^{p}=0. $$

### 2.3. Formal Geometry.

Let $\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})$ be the group scheme of automorphisms of the algebra $A_{0}$ . For any smooth scheme $X$ over $k$ of dimension $2n$ , assigning to a scheme $Z$ over $X^{\prime}$ the set ${\mathcal{M}}_{X}(Z)$ of isomorphisms

$$ Z\times\Spec A_{0}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}Z\times_{X^{\prime}}X $$

of schemes over $Z$ , we get a $\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})$ -torsor over $X^{\prime}$ . Next, let $G_{0}\subset\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})$ be the group subscheme consisting of automorphisms of $A_{0}$ that preserve the restricted Poisson structure on $A_{0}$ . Then the Darboux Lemma above implies that, for every symplectic variety $(X,[\eta])$ with a restricted structure of dimension $2n$ the functor assigning to a scheme $Z$ over $X^{\prime}$ the set ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}(Z)$ of isomorphisms

$$ Z\times\Spec A_{0}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}Z\times_{X^{\prime}}X $$

of restricted Poisson schemes over $Z$ is a $G_{0}$ -torsor over $X^{\prime}$ . Using the faithfully flat descent one gets a bijection between the set of nondegenerate (that is arising from a symplectic form) restricted Poisson structures $[\eta]$ on $X$ and the set of $G_{0}$ -torsors over $X^{\prime}$ equipped with an isomorphism of $\Aut(A_{0})$ -torsors

$$ \underline{\Aut}(A_{0})\times^{G_{0}}{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{M}}_{X}. $$

Lastly, the set of all Frobenius-constant quantizations $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s)$ of $X$ such that the induced Poisson structure on $X$ is nondegenerate is in bijection with the set of torsors ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s}$ over the group scheme $G:=\underline{\Aut}(A_{h})$ of automorphisms of $k[[h]]$ -algebra $A_{h}$ (that is a group scheme whose group of points with values in a $k$ -algebra $R$ is the group of $R[[h]]$ -algebra automorphisms of the $h$ -adically completed tensor product $A_{h}\hat{\otimes}R$ ) together with an isomorphism $\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})$ -torsors

$$ \underline{\Aut}(A_{0})\times^{G}{\mathcal{M}}_{X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{M}}_{X}. $$

In particular, for a symplectic variety with a restricted structure $(X,[\eta])$ , giving a Frobenius constant quantization of $(X,[\eta])$ is equivalent to lifting a $G_{0}$ -torsor ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}$ to a $G$ -torsor ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s}$ along the group scheme homomorphism

$$ G\to G_{0}. $$

### 2.4. Automorphisms of the reduced Weyl algebra.

It is shown in [BK3] that homomorphism (2.4) is surjective and its kernel $G^{\geq 1}$ consists of inner automorphisms. We have the exact sequence

$$ 1\to L^{+}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\to\underline{A}_{h}^{*}\to G\to G_{0}\to 1. $$

Here $\underline{A}_{h}^{*}$ (resp. $L^{+}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ ) is the group scheme over $k$ whose group of $R$ -points is $(R\otimes A_{h})^{*}$ (resp. $R[[h]]^{*}$ ). Letting $G^{\geq n}\subset G$ , ( $n\geq 0$ ), be the group subscheme consisting of automorphisms that are identical modulo $h^{n}$ , we have that $G^{\geq n}/G^{\geq n+1}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\underline{A}_{0}/{\mathbb{G}}_{a}$ for every $n>1$ and $G^{\geq 1}/G^{\geq 2}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\underline{A}_{0}^{*}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ , $G^{\geq 0}/G^{\geq 1}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}G_{0}$ .

Consider the isomorphism of $k[[h]]$ -algebras

$$ \alpha:A_{-h}^{op}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}A_{h} $$

sending $x_{i}$ to $x_{i}$ and $y_{j}$ to $y_{j}$ . The conjugation by $\alpha$ defines an involution $\tau:G\to G$ preserving the subgroups $G^{\geq n}$ , ( $n\geq 0$ ), such that the induced action on $G^{\geq n}/G^{\geq n+1}$ takes an element $g$ to $g^{(-1)^{n}}$ . In particular, it follows that the extension

$$ 1\to G^{\geq 1}/G^{\geq 2}\to G/G^{\geq 2}\to G_{0}\to 1 $$

has a unique ${\mathbb{Z}}/2{\mathbb{Z}}$ -equivariant splitting

$$ G/G^{\geq 2}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}G_{0}\ltimes\underline{A}_{0}^{*}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}. $$

### 2.5. ${\mathbb{Z}}/2{\mathbb{Z}}$ -equivariant structures.

Any ${\mathbb{Z}}/2{\mathbb{Z}}$ -equivariant Frobenius-constant quantization $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s,\alpha)$ is isomorphic locally for the fpqc topology on $X^{\prime}$ to the $h$ -completed tensor product ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}\hat{\otimes}_{k}A_{h}$ equipped with the equivariant structure (2.6). Indeed, consider the action of ${\mathbb{Z}}/2{\mathbb{Z}}$ on $G^{\geq 1}$ given by $\tau$ . Then $H^{1}({\mathbb{Z}}/2{\mathbb{Z}},G^{\geq 1})=0$ as $G^{\geq 1}$ has a filtration $G^{\geq n}$ with uniquely $2$ -divisible quotients. It follows that every two ${\mathbb{Z}}/2{\mathbb{Z}}$ -equivariant structures on ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}\hat{\otimes}_{k}A_{h}$ are locally isomorphic. Now the claim follows from the quantum Darboux Lemma.

Consequently, giving a ${\mathbb{Z}}/2{\mathbb{Z}}$ -equivariant Frobenius constant quantization of $(X,[\eta])$ is equivalent to lifting a $G_{0}$ -torsor ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}$ to a torsor ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s,\alpha}$ over the subgroup $G^{\tau=1}\subset G$ of $\tau$ -invariants.

### 2.6. Construction of quantizations.

Bezrukavnikov and Kaledin use the standard obstruction theory to classify liftings of a given $G_{0}$ -torsor to a $G$ -torsor. Namely, given a $G_{0}$ -torsor ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}$ the set of isomorphism classes of its liftings to a torsor over $G/G^{\geq 2}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}G_{0}\ltimes\underline{A}_{0}^{*}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ is identified with the set of isomorphism classes of torsors over the smooth group scheme $\underline{A}_{0}^{*}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times_{G_{0}}{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}$ over $X^{\prime}$ . The latter group scheme is identified with the quotient of the group scheme of invertible elements in the sheaf of ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}$ -algebras $F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ by constant group scheme ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X^{\prime}$ . Using smoothness of $\underline{A}_{0}^{*}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times_{G_{0}}{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}$ every torsor over this group scheme is locally trivial for the étale topology on $X^{\prime}$ . Hence, the set of isomorphism classes of $\underline{A}_{0}^{*}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times_{G_{0}}{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}$ -torsors is in bijection with $H^{1}_{et}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{p*})$ . This defines a map of sets

$$ \rho:Q(X,[\eta])\to H^{1}_{et}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*p}) $$

from the set $Q(X,[\eta])$ of isomorphisms classes of Frobenius-constant quantizations $(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{h},s)$ compatible with $[\eta]$ to the étale cohomology group classifying torsors over $G_{0}\ltimes\underline{A}_{0}^{*}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ lifting the $G_{0}$ -torsor ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}$ . Note that under this identification the trivial cohomology class corresponds to the lifting obtained from ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}$ via the natural group homomorphism $G_{0}\to G_{0}\ltimes\underline{A}_{0}^{*}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ .

Next, the obstruction class to lifting of a $G/G^{\geq n}$ -torsor, with $n>1$ , to a $G/G^{\geq n+1}$ -torsor lies in $H^{2}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{p})$ . If the obstruction class vanishes then the set of isomorphism classes of the liftings is a torsor over $H^{1}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{p})$ . Hence, if $H^{1}_{Zar}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{p})=0$ then $\rho$ is injective and if $H^{2}_{Zar}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{p})=0$ then $\rho$ is surjective. In particular, if the two cohomology groups vanish $\rho$ is a bijection. The trivial cohomology class corresponds to a quantization that admits (a unique) ${\mathbb{Z}}/2{\mathbb{Z}}$ -equivariant structure.

## 3. Reduction of the main theorem to a group-theoretic statement

In this section we recast the construction of ${\mathcal{D}}_{X,[\eta],h}$ using the language of formal geometry, and reduce Theorem 1 to a certain statement, Proposition 3.3, on central extensions of the group of automorphisms of the restricted Weyl algebra.

### 3.1. ${\mathcal{D}}_{X,[\eta],h}$ via formal geometry.

Let $A_{h}^{\flat}$ be the reduced Weyl algebra in $4n$ variables, that is the $k[[h]]$ -algebra generated by variables $x_{i},y_{i},v_{i},u_{i}$ , $(1\leq i,j,\leq n)$ , subject to the relations

$$ \begin{split}v_{i}x_{j}-x_{j}v_{i}=u_{i}y_{j}-y_{j}u_{i}=\delta_{ij}h,\\
v_{i}y_{j}-y_{j}v_{i}=u_{i}x_{j}-x_{j}u_{i}=v_{i}u_{j}-u_{j}v_{i}=y_{i}x_{j}-x_{j}y_{i}=0\\
x_{i}^{p}=y_{i}^{p}=v_{i}^{p}=u_{i}^{p}=0.\end{split} $$

We shall identify $A_{h}^{\flat}$ with the central reduction $D_{\Spec A_{0},\eta_{A},h}(=D_{\Spec A_{0},0,h})$ , $\eta_{A}=\eta=\sum y_{i}dx_{i}$ , of the algebra $D_{\Spec A_{0},h}\subset D_{\Spec A_{0}}[[h]]$ spanned by $A_{0}$ and $hT_{\Spec A_{0}}$ . In particular, the group scheme $\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})$ acts on $A_{h}^{\flat}$ :

$$ \psi_{can}:\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})\to\underline{\Aut}_{k[[h]]}(A_{h}^{\flat})=:G^{\flat},\quad g\mapsto\psi_{can,g}. $$

We define a homomorphism

$$ \psi:G_{0}\to G^{\flat}, $$

to be the restriction of $\psi_{can}$ to $G_{0}\subset\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})$ twisted by a $1$ -cocycle

$$ G_{0}\to G^{\flat},\quad g\mapsto\phi_{g^{*}\eta-\eta}. $$

Namely, for any $k$ -algebra $R$ , an $R$ -point of $G_{0}$ is an automorphism $g$ of the $R$ -algebra $A_{0}\otimes R$ such that the $1$ -form $\mu:=g^{*}\eta-\eta\in\Omega_{A_{0}\otimes R/R}^{1}$ , $\eta=\sum y_{i}dx_{i}$ , is exact. Let $\phi_{\mu}:A_{h}^{\flat}\hat{\otimes}R\to A_{h}^{\flat}\hat{\otimes}R$ be the $R[[h]]$ -algebra automorphism given by the formulas

$$ \phi_{\mu}(x_{i})=x_{i},\quad\phi_{\mu}(y_{i})=y_{i}, $$

$$ \phi_{\mu}(v_{i})=v_{i}+\iota_{\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{i}}}\mu,\quad\phi_{\mu}(u_{i})=u_{i}+\iota_{\frac{\partial}{\partial y_{i}}}\mu. $$

Define (3.3) by the formula

$$ \psi_{g}=\phi_{g^{*}\eta-\eta}\circ\psi_{can,g}. $$

We claim that (3.3) is a homomorphism. Indeed, one has that

$$ \psi_{can,g}\circ\phi_{\mu}\circ\psi_{can,g}^{-1}=\phi_{g^{*}\mu}. $$

Using this formula we find

## 5. ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant quantizations

In this section we consider quantizations of symplectic varieties $(X,\omega)$ equipped with an action of the multiplicative group ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ such that the form $\omega$ has a positive weight $m$ with respect to this action and $m$ is invertible in $k$ . We recall the notion of a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant Frobenius constant quantization $O_{h}$ of such $(X,\omega)$ . By definition, $O_{h}$ is a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant sheaf of ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}[h]}$ -algebras on $X^{\prime}\times\Spec k[h]$ . In particular, specializing $h=1$ we have a sheaf $O_{h=1}$ of ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}$ -algebras over $X^{\prime}$ . We show that if the action of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ on $X$ is contracting then $O_{h=1}$ is an Azumaya algebra over $X^{\prime}$ and using Theorem 1 compute its class in the Brauer group $\operatorname{Br}(X^{\prime})$ proving a conjecture of Kubrak and Travkin [KT].

### 5.1. Definition of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant quantizations.

Let $X$ be a smooth variety over $k$ equipped with a symplectic $2$ -form $\omega$ and a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -action

$$ \lambda:{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X\to X. $$

We shall say that $\omega$ is of weight $m$ with respect to the ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -action if the following identity holds in $\Gamma({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X,\Omega^{2}_{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}})$

$$ \lambda^{*}\omega=z^{m}\proj_{X}^{*}\omega. $$

Here $z$ denotes the coordinate on ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ and $\proj_{X}:{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X\to X$ the projection. For the duration of this section we shall assume that $\omega$ is of weight $m$ with $m$ invertible in $k$ .

The ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -action on $X$ defines a homomorphism from the Lie algebra of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ to the Lie algebra of vector fields on $X$ . Denote by $\theta$ the image of the generator of $\Lie{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . Formula (5.2) together with the identity $d\omega=0$ imply that

$$ d\iota_{\theta}\omega=m\omega. $$

Hence, setting $\eta=\frac{1}{m}\iota_{\theta}\omega$ , defines a restricted Poisson structure on $X$ . Endow $X^{\prime}[h]\colon=X^{\prime}\times\Spec k[h]$ with the ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -action given by the composition

$$ {\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X^{\prime}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle F\times\Id}}{{\longrightarrow}}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X^{\prime}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\lambda}}{{\longrightarrow}}X^{\prime} $$

(where $F:{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\to{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ is given by $F^{*}(z)=z^{p}$ ) on the first factor and by $h\mapsto z^{m}h$ on the second factor.

A ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant Frobenius-constant quantization of $X$ consists of a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant sheaf $O_{h}$ of associative ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}[h]}$ -algebras on $X^{\prime}[h]$ together with an isomorphism of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}$ -algebras

$$ O_{h}/(h)\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{O}}_{X} $$

such that $O_{h}$ is locally free as an ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}[h]}$ -module and the restriction ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}:=\lim O_{h}/(h^{n})$ of $O_{h}$ to the formal completion of $X^{\prime}[h]$ along the divisor $h=0$ (equipped with the central homomorphism $s:{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[[h]]\to{\mathcal{O}}_{h}$ and (5.3)) is a Frobenius-constant quantization of $X$ compatible with the restricted Poisson structure given by the $1$ -form $\eta=\frac{1}{m}\iota_{\theta}\omega$ .

For example, if $X$ is affine, then a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant Frobenius-constant quantization of $X$ is determined by a graded ${\mathcal{O}}(X^{\prime})[h]$ -algebra $O_{h}(X^{\prime}[h])$ (with $\deg h=m$ ) together with $O_{h}(X^{\prime}[h])/(h)\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{O}}(X)$ .

### 5.2. ${\mathbb{A}}^{1}$ -action.

Below we shall consider ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -actions on a scheme $X$ satisfying the following property: morphism (5.2) extends to a morphism

$$ \tilde{\lambda}:{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\times X\to X. $$

If $X$ is reduced and separated, which we shall assume to be the case for rest of this section, then $\tilde{\lambda}$ defines an action of the monoid ${\mathbb{A}}^{1}$ on $X$ . In particular, the restriction of $\tilde{\lambda}$ to the closed subscheme $X\hookrightarrow{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\times X$ given by the equation $z=0$ factors through the subscheme $X^{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}\hookrightarrow X$ of fixed points:

$$ \tilde{\lambda}_{0}:X\to X^{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\hookrightarrow X. $$

Moreover, $\tilde{\lambda}$ exhibits $X^{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}$ as a ${\mathbb{A}}^{1}$ -homotopy retract of $X$ .

Also note if $X$ is a proper scheme with a nontrivial action of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ then $\tilde{\lambda}$ does not exist. This can be seen by looking at the closure of a $1$ -dimensional ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -orbit in $X$ .

### 5.3. Main result.

By definition a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant Frobenius-constant quantization $O_{h}$ gives rise to a Frobenius-constant quantization ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}$ and thus a class $\rho(O_{h})\in H^{1}_{et}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*p})$ (see §1.4). Denote by $[\rho(O_{h})]\in\operatorname{Br}(X^{\prime})$ the image of $\rho(O_{h})$ under the homomorphism $H^{1}_{et}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*p})\to H^{2}_{et}(X^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}^{*})$ .

Recall from ([OV], §4.2) a homomorphism

$$ \Omega^{1}(X^{\prime})\to\operatorname{Br}(X^{\prime}),\quad\eta\mapsto[\eta] $$

that carries a $1$ -form $\eta$ to the class of the Azumaya algebra $D_{X}$ restricted to the graph of the embedding $\Gamma_{\eta}:X^{\prime}\to{\mathbb{T}}^{*}_{X^{\prime}}$ given by $\eta$ . Finally, denote by $O_{h=1}$ the sheaf of ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}$ -algebras $O_{h}/(h-1)$ . The following result has been conjectured in [KT, §0.3, Question 2].

#### Theorem 5.

Let $X$ be a smooth variety over $k$ equipped equipped with a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -action (5.2) and a symplectic form $\omega$ of weight $m>0$ relatively prime to the characteristic of $k$ . Assume that the morphism (5.1) extends to a morphism (5.4). Then, for every ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant Frobenius-constant quantization $O_{h}$ of $X$ , the restriction of $O_{h}$ to $X^{\prime}[h,h^{-1}]=X^{\prime}\times\Spec k[h,h^{-1}]\subset X^{\prime}[h]$ is an Azumaya algebra. Moreover, the following equality in $\operatorname{Br}(X^{\prime})$ holds

$$ [O_{h=1}]=[\frac{1}{m}\iota_{\theta}\omega]+\tilde{\lambda}_{0}^{*}[\rho(O_{h})]. $$

#### Proof.

To prove the Azumaya property of $O_{h}(h^{-1})$ consider the morphism

$$ \psi:O_{h}\otimes_{{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}[h]}}O_{h}^{op}\to\End_{{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}[h]}}(O_{h}). $$

This is a morphism of vector bundles over $X^{\prime}[h]$ of the same rank. We have to prove that $\psi$ is an isomorphism away from the divisor $h=0$ . Denote by

$$ \det\psi:\wedge^{top}(O_{h}\otimes_{{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}[h]}}O_{h}^{op})\to\wedge^{top}(\End_{{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}[h]}}(O_{h})) $$

the determinant of $\psi$ and by $Z\hookrightarrow X^{\prime}[h]$ . Let $(x_{0},h_{0})\in Z$ be a $k$ -point of $Z$ . We shall check that $h_{0}=0$ . Using (5.4) and the positivity of $m$ the ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -action on $X^{\prime}[h]$ extends to a morphism

$$ \tilde{\lambda}(h):{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\times X^{\prime}[h]\to X^{\prime}[h]. $$

It follows that the closure $T$ of the ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -orbit of $(x_{0},h_{0})$ intersects the divisor $h=0$ at some point $(x_{0}^{\prime},0)$ . Since $Z$ is closed and ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -invariant we have that $T\subset Z$ i.e., $\det\psi$ is identically $0$ on $T$ . On the other hand, using the Azumaya property of the formal quantization ${\mathcal{O}}_{h}(h^{-1})$ we see that the restriction of $\psi$ to the formal punctured neighborhood of $(x_{0}^{\prime},0)\in T$ is an isomorphism. This contradiction proves the first assertion of the Theorem.

For the second one, consider algebra $D_{X,h}$ obtained from the filtered algebra of differential $D_{Y}$ operators via the Rees construction (see §1.2). The $p$ -curvature homomorphism makes $D_{X,h}$ into an algebra over $S^{\cdot}T_{X^{\prime}}[h]$ . The graph $\Gamma_{\eta}:X^{\prime}\rightarrow\mathbb{T}_{X^{\prime}}^{*}$ of the differential form $\eta=\frac{1}{m}\iota_{\theta}\omega$ defines a sheaf of ideals $I_{\Gamma_{\eta}}\subset S^{\cdot}T_{X^{\prime}}$ . The quotient $D_{X,[\eta],h}=D_{X,h}/I_{\Gamma_{\eta}}$ can be viewed as a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant sheaf of ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}[h]}$ -algebras over $X^{\prime}[h]$ . By construction, the restriction of $D_{X,[\eta],h}$ to the formal completion of $X^{\prime}[h]$ along the divisor $h=0$ is isomorphic to the algebra ${\mathcal{D}}_{X,[\eta],h}$ constructed in §1.5. Now given a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant Frobenius-constant quantization $O_{h}$ we consider the tensor product $O_{h}\otimes_{{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[h]}D_{X,[\eta],h}^{op}$ . Using Theorem 1 and the Beauville-Laszlo theorem ([BeLa]) there exists a sheaf $O^{\sharp}_{h}$ of ${\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}[h]}$ -algebras over $X^{\prime}[h]$ whose restriction to $X^{\prime}[h,h^{-1}]$ is $(O_{h}\otimes_{{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[h]}D_{X,[\eta],h}^{op})(h^{-1})$ and whose restriction to the formal completion of $X^{\prime}[h]$ along the divisor $h=0$ is an Azumaya algebra. It follows that $O^{\sharp}_{h}$ is an Azumaya algebra over $X^{\prime}[h]$ . We claim that the following equality holds in $\operatorname{Br}({\mathbb{A}}^{1}\times X^{\prime}[h])$

$$ \tilde{\lambda}(h)^{*}([O^{\sharp}_{h}])=\proj^{*}_{X^{\prime}[h]}([O^{\sharp}_{h}]). $$

Indeed, since $(O_{h}\otimes_{{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}[h]}D_{X,[\eta],h}^{op})(h^{-1})$ is ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant the equality holds after the restriction to ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X^{\prime}[h,h^{-1}]$ . Now the claim follows from the injectivity of the restriction morphism $\operatorname{Br}({\mathbb{A}}^{1}\times X^{\prime}[h])\to\operatorname{Br}({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X^{\prime}[h,h^{-1}])$ . Restricting the classes in (5.7) to the divisor $X^{\prime}[h]\stackrel{{\scriptstyle z=0}}{{\longrightarrow}}{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\times X^{\prime}[h]$ we find that

$$ \tilde{\lambda}(h)^{*}_{0}([O^{\sharp}_{h}])=[O^{\sharp}_{h}]. $$

Morphism $\tilde{\lambda}(h)^{*}_{0}:X^{\prime}[h]\to X^{\prime}[h]$ factors as follows

$$ X^{\prime}[h]\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\proj_{X^{\prime}}}}{{\longrightarrow}}X^{\prime}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\tilde{\lambda}(h)^{*}_{0}}}{{\longrightarrow}}X^{\prime}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle h=0}}{{\longrightarrow}}X^{\prime}[h]. $$

By Theorem 1 the restriction of $[O^{\sharp}_{h}]$ to the divisor $X^{\prime}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle h=0}}{{\longrightarrow}}X^{\prime}[h]$ is equal to $[\rho(O_{h})]$ . Using (5.8) and restricting to the divisor $h=1$ we find that

$$ [O^{\sharp}_{h=1}]=[\rho(O_{h})] $$

as desired.

### 6.1. The affine grassmannian for ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ .

Let $G$ be an algebraic group over a field $k$ . Denote by

$$ LG:\text{Aff}_{k}^{op}\to\text{Groups} $$

the corresponding loop group, that is a sheaf of groups on the category of affine schemes over $k$ equipped with the fpqc topology sending $k$ -scheme $\Spec R$ to $G(R((h)))$ . Also, let

$$ L^{+}G:\text{Aff}_{k}^{op}\to\text{Groups} $$

be the sheaf of groups sending $k$ -scheme $\Spec R$ to $G(R[[h]])$ . It is known (e.g. see [Zhu, Proposition 1.3.2] ) that $L^{+}G$ is represented by a group scheme over $k$ and that $LG$ is an ind-affine scheme. Denote by $\Gra_{G}$ the affine grassmannian for $G$ . By definition, $\Gra_{G}$ is the fpqc sheaf associated to the presheaf $R\mapsto LG(R)/L^{+}G(R)$ .

Recall the structure of the affine grassmannian for ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . The following result is well-known (see, for example, [CC]); for the reader’s convenience we include its proof.

#### Lemma 6.1.

For a commutative ring $R$ such that $\Spec R$ is connected there is a decomposition

$$ R((h))^{*}=R^{*}\times{\mathbb{W}}(R)\times\mathbb{Z}\times\hat{\mathbb{W}}(R), $$

where ${\mathbb{W}}(R)$ is the subgroup of $R[[h]]^{*}$ formed by formal power series with constant term $1$ , $\hat{\mathbb{W}}(R)$ is the group of polynomials of the form $1+\Sigma a_{i}h^{-i}$ with nilpotent coefficients $a_{i}\in R$ . In addition, we have that

$$ \hat{\mathbb{W}}(R)=\ker(R[h^{-1}]^{*}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle f\mapsto f(0)}}{{\longrightarrow}}R^{*}). $$

#### Proof.

The claim follows from the fact that under the assumptions of the lemma

$$ R((h))^{*}=\left\{\sum_{i}a_{i}h^{i}\in R((h));\exists i_{0}:a_{i_{0}}\in R^{*},a_{j}\text{ nilpotent for all }j<i_{0}\right\}. $$

To show this replace $R$ by $R/\mathfrak{N}_{R}$ , where $\mathfrak{N}_{R}$ stands for the nilradical. We need to show that a Laurent polynomial is invertible if and only if its first nonzero coefficient is invertible in $R$ . Suppose that

$$ A(h)B(h)=1 $$

for $A(h),B(h)\in R((h))$ such that

$$ \begin{split}A(h)=a_{-N}h^{-N}+a_{-N+1}h^{-N+1}+...\\
B(h)=b_{-N}h^{-M}+b_{-M+1}h^{-M+1}+...\end{split}{} $$

where $b_{-M}\neq 0$ and $a_{-N}\neq 0$ . From (6.1) we have that $N+M\geq 0$ . If $N+M=0$ then $a_{-N}b_{-M}=1$ and we are done. Otherwise, we have from (6.1)

$$ a_{-N}b_{-M}=0,\quad a_{-N}b_{-M+1}+a_{-N+1}b_{-M}=0,\cdots $$

$$ a_{-N}b_{-M+(N+M)}+\ldots+a_{-N+(N+M)}b_{-M}=1. $$

Using (6.3) we get $a_{-N}^{2}b_{-M+1}=0$ and similarly $a_{-N}^{i}b_{-M+i}=0$ for every $i\leq N+M$ . Multiplying both sides of (6.4) by $a_{-N}^{N+M}$ we infer

$$ a_{-N}^{N+M}(1-a_{-N}b_{-M+(N+M)})=0. $$

Since $a_{-N}$ and $1-a_{-N}b_{-M+(N+M)}$ are coprime:

$$ R\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}R/(a_{-N})\times R/(1-a_{-N}b_{-M+(N+M)}), $$

$\Spec R$ is connected, and $a_{-N}\neq 0$ we conclude that $1-a_{-N}b_{-M+(N+M)}=0$ . Hence $a_{-N}$ is invertible as desired. ∎

Using the Lemma, we have decompositions

$$ L{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times{\mathbb{W}}\times\underline{{\mathbb{Z}}}\times\hat{\mathbb{W}}, $$

$$ \Gra_{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\underline{{\mathbb{Z}}}\times\hat{\mathbb{W}}, $$

where ${\mathbb{W}}$ is the group scheme of big Witt vectors and $\hat{\mathbb{W}}$ is a group ind-scheme whose group of $R$ -points is defined in the Lemma.

### 6.2. Subgroups of $L\GL(n)$ .

#### Proposition 6.2.

Let $G$ be an affine group scheme over a field $k$ , and let $\phi:G\to LGL(n)$ be a homomorphism. Then there exists an element $g\in GL(n,k((h)))$ such that $\phi$ factors through $gL^{+}GL(n)g^{-1}$ :

$$ G\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\phi}}{{\longrightarrow}}g(L^{+}GL(n))g^{-1}\hookrightarrow LGL(n). $$

#### Proof.

Set $V=k^{n}$ . We have to show that there exists a $\phi(G)$ -invariant $k[[h]]$ -lattice

$$ \Lambda\subset V((h)). $$

Informally, our $\Lambda$ will be constructed starting with the lattice $\Lambda_{0}=V[[h]]$ as the intersection $\bigcap_{g}g\Lambda_{0}$ . Since we make no assumptions on $k$ and $G$ one has give a meaning to the latter. We shall do it as follows.

The morphism $\phi$ is given by a matrix $A\in\GL(n,{\mathcal{O}}(G)((h)))$ such that

$$ A\otimes A=\Delta(A)\in\GL(n,({\mathcal{O}}(G)\otimes{\mathcal{O}}(G))((h))), $$

where $\Delta:{\mathcal{O}}(G)\to{\mathcal{O}}(G)\otimes{\mathcal{O}}(G)$ is the comultiplication on ${\mathcal{O}}(G)$ given by the product morphism $G\times G\to G$ and such that the image of $A$ under the evaluation at $1\in G(k)$ homomorphism $\GL(n,{\mathcal{O}}(G)((h)))\to\GL(n,k((h)))$ is the identity matrix.

Set

$$ \Lambda=\{v\in V((h))\;\text{such\, that}\;Av\in V\otimes_{k}{\mathcal{O}}(G)[[h]]\}. $$

Then $\Lambda$ is a $k[[h]]$ -submodule of $V[[h]]$ contains $h^{N}V[[h]]$ , for sufficiently large $N$ . Hence, $\Lambda$ is a lattice. It remains to show that $\Lambda$ is $\phi(G)$ -invariant, that is

$$ A(\Lambda)\subset\Lambda\otimes_{k[[h]]}{\mathcal{O}}(G)[[h]]. $$

The matrix $A$ defines ${\mathcal{O}}(G)((h))$ -linear maps

$$ \begin{split}V((h))\otimes_{k[[h]]}{\mathcal{O}}(G)[[h]]\stackrel{{\scriptstyle A\otimes\Id}}{{\longrightarrow}}(V((h))\otimes_{k[[h]]}{\mathcal{O}}(G)[[h]])\otimes_{k[[h]]}{\mathcal{O}}(G)[[h]]\to\\
\to V((h))\otimes_{k[[h]]}({\mathcal{O}}(G)\otimes_{k}{\mathcal{O}}(G))[[h]],\end{split} $$

where the second map in (6.6) is induced by the embedding

$$ {\mathcal{O}}(G)[[h]]\otimes_{k[[h]]}{\mathcal{O}}(G)[[h]]\to({\mathcal{O}}(G)\otimes_{k}{\mathcal{O}}(G))[[h]]. $$

Since the cokernel of (6.7) and ${\mathcal{O}}(G)[[h]]$ are both flat $k[[h]]$ -modules it follows that $\Lambda\otimes_{k[[h]]}{\mathcal{O}}(G)[[h]]$ is precisely the preimage of $V[[h]]\otimes_{k[[h]]}({\mathcal{O}}(G)\otimes_{k}{\mathcal{O}}(G))[[h]]$ under the composition (6.6).

Hence it suffices to check that (6.6) carries $A(\Lambda)$ to $V[[h]]\otimes_{k[[h]]}({\mathcal{O}}(G)\otimes_{k}{\mathcal{O}}(G))[[h]].$ But the composition

$$ V((h))\stackrel{{\scriptstyle A}}{{\longrightarrow}}V((h))\otimes_{k[[h]]}{\mathcal{O}}(G)[[h]]\stackrel{{\scriptstyle(\ref{eqprodmatcompbis})}}{{\longrightarrow}}V((h))\otimes_{k[[h]]}({\mathcal{O}}(G)\otimes_{k}{\mathcal{O}}(G))[[h]] $$

is equal to

$$ V((h))\stackrel{{\scriptstyle A}}{{\longrightarrow}}V((h))\otimes_{k[[h]]}{\mathcal{O}}(G)[[h]]\stackrel{{\scriptstyle Id\otimes\Delta}}{{\longrightarrow}}V((h))\otimes_{k[[h]]}({\mathcal{O}}(G)\otimes_{k}{\mathcal{O}}(G))[[h]] $$

by (6.5). Hence it carries $\Lambda$ to $V[[h]]\otimes_{k[[h]]}({\mathcal{O}}(G)\otimes_{k}{\mathcal{O}}(G))[[h]]$ and we win. ∎

The analogues assertion for $L\PGL(n)$ does not hold.

$$ H\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\lim_{\longleftarrow}H/H^{\geq i} $$

and every quotient $H/H^{\geq i}$ is unipotent (i.e., has a finite composition series with all quotient groups isomorphic to the additive group ${\mathbb{G}}_{a}$ ).

#### Proposition 6.5.

Let $G$ be an affine group scheme over a perfect field $k$ , and let $\phi:G\to L\PGL(n)$ be a homomorphism. Assume that $G$ has a normal pro-unipotent group subscheme $G^{\geq 1}\subset G$ such that $\phi(G^{\geq 1})\subset L^{+}\PGL(n)$ and the quotient $G_{0}=G/G^{\geq 1}$ has finite type over $k$ . - (ii) The following two conditions are equivalent. (1) There exists an element $g\in\PGL(n,k((h)))$ such that $\phi$ factors through $gL^{+}\PGL(n)g^{-1}$ :

$$ G\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\phi}}{{\longrightarrow}}g(L^{+}PGL(n))g^{-1}\hookrightarrow LPGL(n). $$

(2) The extension (6.10)

$$ 1\to L{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\to\tilde{G}\to G\to 1 $$

admits a reduction $\tilde{G}^{+}$ to $L^{+}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ .

$$ \begin{matrix}1&\to&L^{+}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}&\to&\tilde{G}^{+}&\to&G&\to&1\cr&&\Big\downarrow\hbox to0.0pt{$\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle$}}$\hss}&&\Big\downarrow\hbox to0.0pt{$\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle$}}$\hss}&&\Big\downarrow\hbox to0.0pt{$\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle\Id$}}$\hss}&&\cr 1&\to&L{\mathbb{G}}_{m}&\to&\tilde{G}&\to&G&\to&1\end{matrix} $$

For part (i) observe that the morphism of schemes

$$ L^{+}\GL(n)\to L^{+}\PGL(n) $$

admits a section locally for the Zariski topology on $L^{+}PGL(n)$ . Also since every $G^{\geq 1}$ -torsor over an affine scheme is trivial the projection

$$ G\twoheadrightarrow G_{0} $$

admits a scheme-theoretic section $s:G_{0}\to G$ . Hence it suffices to check that the composition $G_{0}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle s}}{{\longrightarrow}}G\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\phi}}{{\longrightarrow}}L\PGL(n)$ lifts locally for the Zariski topology on $G_{0}$ to scheme-theoretic morphism $G_{0}\to L\GL(n)$ . Set $G_{0}=\Spec R$ . Then $\phi\circ s$ defines a morphism

$$ \Spec R((h))\to\PGL(n). $$

The pullback of the ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -torsor $\GL(n)\to\PGL(n)$ defines a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -torsor $L$ over $\Spec R((h))$ . Observe that $\phi\circ s$ admits a lifting to $L\GL(n)$ if and only if $L$ is trivial. Thus to complete the proof of (i) we have to show that there exists an affine open covering $\Spec R=\cup U_{i}$ such that the pullback of $L$ to $\Spec{\mathcal{O}}(U_{i})((h))$ is trivial for every $i$ . We shall prove a stronger assertion: the morphism $\Spec R((h))\to\Spec R$ induces an isomorphism

$$ \Pic(R)\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\Pic(R((h))). $$

Since $G_{0}$ is a group scheme and $k$ is perfect, the reduction $R_{red}$ is smooth over $k$ . Since $R$ is a finitely generated $k$ -algebra, the kernel of the projection $R\to R_{red}$ is a nilpotent ideal. It follows that $(R((h))_{red}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}R_{red}((h))$ . Consequently, we have that

$$ \Pic(R)\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\Pic(R_{red}),\quad\Pic(R((h)))\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\Pic(R_{red}((h))). $$

Next, using regularity of $R_{red}((h))$ we conclude that

$$ \Pic(R_{red}((h)))\cong\Class(R_{red}((h)))\cong\Class(R_{red}[[h]])\cong\Pic(R_{red}[[h]])\cong\Pic(R_{red}). $$

This proves part (i).

For part (ii), let $\tilde{G}^{+}$ be a reduction of $\tilde{G}$ to $L^{+}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . Since $L^{+}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ is an affine group scheme (as opposed to merely a group ind-scheme) $\tilde{G}^{+}$ is also an affine group scheme. Applying Proposition 6.2 we conclude that the homomorphism $\tilde{G}^{+}\to L\GL(n)$ factors through $gL^{+}\GL(n)g^{-1}$ , for some $g\in\GL(n,k((h)))$ . Hence $G\to L\PGL(n)$ factors through $gL^{+}\PGL(n)g^{-1}$ . The inverse implication is clear.

Finally, for part (iii), set $\bar{G}:=\tilde{G}/L^{+}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . We have to show that the central extension

$$ \Gra_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}\to\bar{G}\to G $$

admits a unique splitting. We shall first construct a scheme-theoretic section of the projection $\bar{G}\to G$ . Using part (i) there exists an open cover $G=\cup U_{i}$ and sections $s_{i}:U_{i}\to\tilde{G}$ of the projection $\tilde{G}\to G$ . Let $\bar{s}_{i}:U_{i}\to\bar{G}$ be the composition of $s_{i}$ with the quotient map $\tilde{G}\to\bar{G}$ . Since $G$ is reduced the morphisms

$$ \bar{s}_{i}\bar{s}_{j}^{-1}:U_{i}\cap U_{j}\to\Gra_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}=\hat{\mathbb{W}}\times{\mathbb{Z}} $$

lands at the second factor. Hence the collection $\{\bar{s}_{i}\bar{s}_{j}^{-1}\}$ defines a Čech $1$ -cocycle for the constant sheaf ${\mathbb{Z}}$ on $G$ . Since $G$ is irreducible, we have that $\check{H}^{1}(G,\mathbb{Z})=0$ . Thus, we have a global scheme-theoretic section $\bar{s}:G\to\bar{G}$ of the projection $\bar{G}\to G$ . We claim that every such section satisfying $\bar{s}(1)=1$ is a group homomorphism. To see this it suffices to show that the diagram

$$ \begin{matrix}G\times G&\stackrel{{\scriptstyle m}}{{\longrightarrow}}&G\cr\Big\downarrow\hbox to0.0pt{$\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle\bar{s}\times\bar{s}$}}$\hss}&&\Big\downarrow\hbox to0.0pt{$\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle\bar{s}$}}$\hss}\cr\bar{G}\times\bar{G}&\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\bar{m}}}{{\longrightarrow}}&\bar{G}\end{matrix} $$

is commutative. In turn, this follows from the fact that every scheme-theoretic morphism from a connected reduced scheme to $\Gra_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}$ is constant. ∎

### 6.4. A representation of $\lsp(2n)$ .

In this subsection we prove irreducibility of a certain representation of the Lie algebra $\lsp(2n)$ that we used in the proof of Lemma 4.3. We use notations from §4.1.

#### Lemma 6.6.

For every integer $l$ with $0\leq l<2(p-1)$ , the adjoint representation of the Lie algebra $\lsp(2n)=m^{2}/m^{3}$ on $m^{l}/m^{l+1}$ is irreducible.

#### Proof.

Write $m_{n}^{l}/m_{n}^{l+1}$ for $m^{k}/m^{k+1}$ . It is easy to verify the assertion of the lemma for $n=1$ : in fact, the representation of $\lsp(2)=m_{1}/m_{1}^{2}$ on $m_{1}^{l}/m_{1}^{l+1}$ is irreducible for every $l\geq 0$ . Moreover, the representations $m_{1}^{l}/m_{1}^{l+1}$ and $m_{1}^{l^{\prime}}/m_{1}^{l^{\prime}+1}$ are isomorphic if and only if $l+l^{\prime}=2p-2$ .

To prove the lemma in general, consider the restriction of the representation of $\lsp(2n)$ on $m_{n}^{l}/m_{n}^{l+1}$ to the Lie subalgebra

$$ \lsp(2)^{\oplus^{n}}\hookrightarrow\lsp(2n) $$

of the block diagonal matrices. The latter representation decomposes as follows

$$ m^{l}_{n}/m_{n}^{l+1}=\bigoplus_{i_{1}+\ldots+i_{n}=l}m_{1}^{i_{1}}/m_{1}^{i_{1}+1}\otimes\ldots\otimes m_{1}^{i_{n}}/m_{1}^{i_{n}+1}. $$

By the Jacobson density theorem the representation of $\lsp(2)^{\oplus^{n}}$ on each summand is irreducible. Moreover, if $l<2(p-1)$ then these direct summands are pairwise non-isomorphic. It follows that any subspace $V\subset m^{l}_{n}/m_{n}^{l+1}$ invariant under the $\lsp(2)^{\oplus^{n}}$ -action is the sum of some of the summands appearing in (6.13). Hence, it suffices to prove that if a $\lsp(2n)$ -subrepresentatioin $W\subset m^{l}_{n}/m_{n}^{l+1}$ contains $m_{1}^{i_{1}}/m_{1}^{i_{1}+1}\otimes\ldots\otimes m_{1}^{i_{n}}/m_{1}^{i_{n}+1}$ , for some partition $(i_{1},\ldots,i_{n})$ of $l$ with $i_{1}>0$ , the projection of $W$ to $m_{1}^{i_{1}-1}/m_{1}^{i_{1}}\otimes m_{1}^{i_{2}+1}/m_{1}^{i_{2}+2}\otimes\ldots\otimes m_{1}^{i_{n}}/m_{1}^{i_{n}+1}$ is nonzero. This reduces the proof to the case $n=2$ which is shown by direct inspection. ∎
